answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. So the design does not rely on catching every cheat — it makes cheating unprofitable, which is a far more stable defense than any whitelist ever could be. Consider a karst as the anchor of the cost. A wharf stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a pearl...
